title: Lobby — a concierge for humans and their agents
pitch: Lobby gives any business an AI concierge on its website. With WebMCP, the embed also exposes the concierge as structured tools — whatever a guest can do, a visiting agent can do too.
about_excerpt: Lobby gives any business an AI concierge on its website. With WebMCP, the embed also exposes the concierge as structured tools — whatever a guest can do, a visiting agent can do too. Like Comment Story Updates Inspiration Every business answers the same questions all day — "are you open?", "how do I book?", "do you do private events?". Lobby started as an answer to that: a concierge any business can put on its website that actually knows the business and speaks with its guests. But guests are changing. More and more of them don't browse — they send their agent. A person asks ChatGPT or Claude to "find me a tennis lesson in Miami on Thursday," and the agent goes out to the web to figure it out by scraping pages and guessing at UIs. The businesses we serve are exactly the ones agents struggle with most: small, local, with information living in a conversation rather than structured markup. Our thesis from day one: the concierge should be one gate with two doors — one for humans, one for their agents. WebMCP is the missing piece that makes the second door real. What it does Lobby gives any business an AI concierge at lobby.host/c/<business> and as an embeddable widget on the business's own site (text + voice). With WebMCP, every page that carries a Lobby concierge now also registers structured tools for visiting agents: ask_concierge — ask the business's concierge anything a guest could ask; the reply comes from the same knowledge and logic the human-facing chat uses get_business_info — structured facts: hours, location, services, pricing, policies list_offerings — what the business offers, as data an agent can compare across businesses The point is symmetry: whatever a guest can do through the concierge, a visiting agent can do through the tools — same backend, same knowledge, same conversation engine. A human browsing with their agent can let the agent pre-ask the boring questions, then take over the conversation themselves in the same widget. One integration, many businesses: because the tools live in the Lobby embed, every business that installs Lobby becomes agent-accessible without writing a line of code. How we built it WebMCP layer (new, built during the challenge): an open-source script that ships with the Lobby widget and registers the tools via navigator.modelContext / document.modelContext.registerTool() . Tool schemas are generated from the concierge's public API, so any concierge slug works. Concierge platform (pre-existing): NestJS + PostgreSQL backend on Railway, Next.js frontend on Vercel, SSE streaming for replies, OpenAI for voice (TTS/STT). In line with the challenge rules on pre-existing work: the Lobby platform predates the challenge; everything WebMCP — the tool layer, its repo, and the demo integration — was built during the submission period, and the repo README documents the boundary between the two. Challenges we ran into Designing tools that are useful to an agent without letting it bypass the business's own boundaries — the tools expose exactly what the human-facing concierge exposes, nothing more. Making one tool surface work for both "agent browsing alongside a human" and "agent acting for an absent human" — the shared-session UX took the most iteration. Testing across ChatGPT's in-app browser and Chrome with WebMCP enabled, which behave differently enough to matter. What's next Bookings and transactions: the next set of tools lets an agent not just ask, but do — check availability and book, through the same permissioned gate. Lobby becomes the way a small business plugs into the agentic web without rebuilding anything. live_observation.first_impression: A branded ARENNA business page lists concierge capabilities and common questions, with options to talk or type.
live_observation.action_attempted: Opened the text concierge using Type instead.
live_observation.after_state: A chat panel opened with suggested questions, a reply textbox, and send controls.
live_observation.notes: The concierge flow was clearly exposed, though no question was submitted.
